_comment: Issue #3694: which queried addresses get DDR designations. A public IPv6 address gets none (a global prefix changes, so a certificate cannot keep an IP SAN for it); an IPv4 address, an IPv4-mapped one (classified by its IPv4 address) and a non-public IPv6 address are designated as ever. Read by tests/php/DdrPublicIpv6ParityTest.php (PHP's PFB_DNS_PROXY_NON_PUBLIC and its certificate warning) and go/pfb_dns_gateway/ddr_public_ipv6_test.go (the gateway's designations), so the two cannot drift. `ranges` are the IPv6 entries of PFB_DNS_PROXY_NON_PUBLIC, in order; `public` is what pfb_dns_proxy_public_address() says; `ddr` is whether the gateway designates on the address. The wider IPv6 ranges have their first and last address and the address on each side.
_note: `::` is not an address a client queries (a socket on it reports the wildcard), so it has no row; ::/128 stays in `ranges`.
